blocks.prompt: 6. Show that the ratio of the sum of first \(n\) terms of a G.P. to the sum of terms from \((n + 1)\)th to \((2n)\)th term is \(\frac{1}{r^{n}}\), where \(r\) is the common ratio of G.P.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh proof hai. Ahem baat: \((n+1)\)th se \((2n)\)th tak ke terms khud ek G.P. hain jis mein \(n\) terms hain aur ratio wohi \(r\) hai.
Plan: dono sums G.P. ke formula se likh kar divide karenge (\(r \neq 1\) aur \(r^{n} \neq 1\) maan kar, taake koi cheez zero na ho; \(r = 1\) par dono sums \(na_1\) hain aur ratio \(1 = \frac{1}{1^{n}}\) phir bhi sahi hai).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: G.P. \(a_1, a_1 r, a_1 r^{2}, \ldots\)
Saabit karna hai: \(\dfrac{S_n}{a_{n+1} + \cdots + a_{2n}} = \dfrac{1}{r^{n}}\).
Tareeqa: Dono hisson ke liye sum ka formula \(\frac{a_1(1 - r^{n})}{1 - r}\) istemal karenge. Doosre hisse ke liye bas us ka pehla term badal jata hai.

Pehle \(n\) terms ka sum
\[S_n = \dfrac{a_1(1 - r^{n})}{1 - r}\]
Kyun: Yeh G.P. ke sum ka seedha formula hai.

Doosre group ke terms
\[a_{n+1} = a_1 r^{n}\]
\[a_{n+1} + \cdots + a_{2n} = \dfrac{a_1 r^{n}(1 - r^{n})}{1 - r}\]
Kyun: General term \(a_k = a_1 r^{k-1}\) se \(a_{n+1} = a_1 r^{n}\). \((n+1)\)th se \((2n)\)th tak \(2n - n = n\) terms hain, aur har term pichle ka \(r\) guna hai. Is liye yeh G.P. hai jis ka pehla term \(a_1 r^{n}\), ratio \(r\), aur \(n\) terms.
Dhyan dein: Terms ginte waqt \(2n - (n + 1) = n - 1\) mat ginye; dono kinaare shamil hain, is liye \(n\) terms hain.

Divide karein
\[\dfrac{S_n}{a_{n+1} + \cdots + a_{2n}} = \dfrac{a_1(1 - r^{n})}{a_1 r^{n}(1 - r^{n})}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{r^{n}}\]
Kyun: Dono ka denominator \(1 - r\) ek jaisa hai, cancel ho gaya. Phir upar neeche \(a_1\) aur \((1 - r^{n})\) bhi cancel; sirf neeche \(r^{n}\) bacha.

Tasdeeq: numbers se
\[1, 2, 4, 8:\ \ n = 2,\ r = 2\]
\[\dfrac{1 + 2}{4 + 8} = \dfrac{3}{12} = \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2^{2}}\]
Kyun: Pehle do terms ka sum 3, agle do ka 12; ratio \(\frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{r^{n}}\). Asaan alfaaz mein: doosre group ka har term pehle group ke mutabiq term ka \(r^{n}\) guna hai, is liye poora sum bhi \(r^{n}\) guna hai.
